[[File:Hachioji Jinjya.JPG|250px|thumb|Hachioji Shrine at Fukazawa Mountain (Hachioji City)]]
'''Hachioji Shrine''' (八王子神社) enshrines the {{ill|Hachioji Gongen|ja|八王子権現|qid=Q11391615|lt=Eight Princes (Hachioji Gongen)}} (八柱の御子神) of {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|en|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}} (also known as {{ill|Gozu Tennō|en|Gozu Tennō|qid=Q11570247|lt=Gozu Tennō}}). It is also referred to as '''Hachioji-miya''' or '''Yahashira Shrine''' (八柱神社), and there are numerous such shrines across Japan.

== Overview ==

Hachioji Shrines originated from the syncretic belief in {{ill|Hachioji Gongen|ja|八王子権現|qid=Q11391615}} under the system of {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|en|Shinbutsu-shūgō|qid=Q2279088|lt=Shinbutsu-shūgō}}. 

In {{ill|913|ab|913|af|913|am|913 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|913|ar|913|ary|913|arz|913|ast|913|avk|913|az|913|azb|۹۱۳ (میلادی)|bcl|913|be|913|be_x_old|913|bg|913|bn|৯১৩|bpy|মারি ৯১৩|br|913|bs|913.|ca|913|cdo|913 nièng|ceb|913|ckb|٩١٣|crh|913|cs|913|csb|913|cv|913|cy|913|da|913|de|913|el|913|eml|913|eo|913|es|913|et|913|eu|913|fa|۹۱۳ (میلادی)|fi|913|fo|913|fr|913|fy|913|ga|913|gan|913年|gd|913|gl|913|he|913|hi|913|hr|913.|ht|913 (almanak jilyen)|hu|913|hy|913|id|913|ilo|913|io|913|is|913|it|913|ja|913年|jv|913|ka|913|kaa|913|kk|913 жыл|ko|913년|la|913|lb|913|lij|913|lmo|913|lt|913 m.|lv|913. gads|map_bms|913|mdf|913|mg|913|mhr|913|mi|913|mk|913|mr|इ.स. ९१३|mrj|913 и|ms|913|mzn|۹۱۳|nah|913|nap|913|nds|913|new|सन् ९१३|nl|913|nn|913|no|913|nrm|913|nso|913|oc|913|or|୯୧୩|os|913-æм аз|pl|913|pnb|913|pt|913|qu|913|ro|913|ru|913 год|rue|913|sa|९१३|scn|913|sd|913ع|se|913|sh|913.|shn|913|si|913|sk|913|sl|913|smn|913|sq|913|sr|913|su|913|sv|913|sw|913|tg|Соли 913|th|พ.ศ. 1456|tk|913|tl|913|tly|913|tr|913|tt|913 ел|uk|913|ur|913ء|uz|913|vec|913|vi|913|war|913|wuu|913年|xmf|913|zh|913年|zh_min_nan|913 nî|zh_yue|913年|qid=Q24860|lt=913}}, Buddhist monk Kegon Bosatsu Myōgyō had a vision of Gozu Tennō and eight princes while practicing asceticism at Fukazawa Mountain, currently {{ill|Mount Shiroyama|ja|城山 (八王子市)|lld|Mont Shiroyama|qid=Q11426084}} in {{ill|Hachiōji|en|Hachiōji|qid=Q208863|lt=Hachioji City}}, Tokyo. Inspired by this revelation, he enshrined {{ill|Hachioji Gongen|ja|八王子権現|qid=Q11391615}} at Fukazawa Mountain in {{ill|916|ab|916|af|916|am|916 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|916|ar|916|ary|916|arz|916|ast|916|avk|916|az|916|azb|۹۱۶ (میلادی)|bcl|916|be|916|be_x_old|916|bg|916|bn|৯১৬|bpy|মারি ৯১৬|br|916|bs|916.|ca|916|cdo|916 nièng|ceb|916|ckb|٩١٦|crh|916|cs|916|csb|916|cv|916|cy|916|da|916|de|916|el|916|eml|916|eo|916|es|916|et|916|eu|916|fa|۹۱۶ (میلادی)|fi|916|fo|916|fr|916|fy|916|ga|916|gan|916年|gd|916|gl|916|he|916|hi|916|ht|916 (almanak jilyen)|hu|916|hy|916|id|916|ilo|916|io|916|is|916|it|916|ja|916年|jv|916|ka|916|kaa|916|kk|916 жыл|ko|916년|la|916|lb|916|lij|916|lmo|916|lt|916 m.|lv|916. gads|map_bms|916|mdf|916|mg|916|mhr|916|mi|916|mk|916|mr|इ.स. ९१६|mrj|916 и|ms|916|mzn|۹۱۶|nah|916|nap|916|nds|916|new|सन् ९१६|nl|916|nn|916|no|916|nrm|916|nso|916|oc|916|or|୯୧୬|os|916-æм аз|pl|916|pnb|916|pt|916|qu|916|ro|916|ru|916 год|rue|916|sa|९१६|scn|916|sd|916ع|se|916|sh|916.|shn|916|si|916|sk|916|sl|916|smn|916|sq|916|sr|916|su|916|sv|916|sw|916|tg|Соли 916|th|พ.ศ. 1459|tk|916|tl|916|tly|916|tr|916|tt|916 ел|uk|916|ur|916ء|uz|916|vec|916|vi|916|war|916|wuu|916年|xmf|916|zh|916年|zh_min_nan|916 nî|zh_yue|916年|qid=Q24886|lt=916}}.

Gozu Tennō, regarded as a Buddhist guardian deity, is believed to have had eight children with {{ill|Harisai-sho|ja|頗梨采女|zh|頗梨采女|qid=Q1654753}}. These children are enshrined as the Hachioji deities.

The eight princes were later associated with eight directions and calendar deities, also known as {{ill|Hasshōshin|ja|八将神|zh|八將神|qid=Q603995}}:
* {{ill|Taisai-shin|ja|太歳神|zh|太歲神|qid=Q10941586}} (Jupiter, Sōkō Tennō)
* {{ill|Daishōgun|ja|大将軍 (方位神)|lt=Daishōgun}} (Venus, Maō Tennō)
* {{ill|Taion-shin|ja|太陰神}} (Saturn, Kumara Tennō)
* {{ill|Saigyōshin|ja|歳刑神}} (Mercury, Tokutatsu Tennō)
* {{ill|Saiha Shin|ja|歳破神}} (Saturn, Ryōji Tennō)
* {{ill|Saisetsujin|ja|歳殺神}} (Mars, Jishin Tennō)
* {{ill|Ōbanjin|ja|黄幡神}} (Rahu, Takushin Tennō)
* {{ill|Hyōbijin|ja|豹尾神}} (Ketu, Jakidokikami Tennō)

During the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|en|Shinbutsu bunri|qid=Q1970535|lt=Shinbutsu bunri}} of the Meiji era, the eight princes were redefined as the {{ill|Five Male and Three Female Deities|ja|五男三女神}}, born from the {{ill|Oath|ja|誓約|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ukei|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 宣誓|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q381045}} between {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|アマテラス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q455602}} and Susanoo:
* {{ill|Ame-no-oshihomimi|de|Amenooshihomimi|fa|آمه-نو-اوشیهومیمی|fr|Ame-no-oshihomimi|it|Ame-no-oshihomimi|ja|アメノオシホミミ|ko|아메노오시호미미|mni|ꯑꯃꯦ-ꯅꯣ-ꯑꯣꯁꯤꯍꯣꯃꯤꯃꯤ|ru|Амэноосихомими но Микото|th|อาเมะ โนะ โอชิโฮมิมิ|uk|Аменоосіхомімі но Мікото|zh|天忍穗耳尊|qid=Q462555}}
* {{ill|Ame-no-Hohi|ja|天之菩卑能命}}
* {{ill|Amatsuhikone|ja|天津日子根命}}
* {{ill|Ikutsuhikone|ja|活津日子根命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikutsuhikone|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イクツヒコネ|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11147583}}
* {{ill|Kumanokusubi|ja|熊野久須毘命}}
* {{ill|Takiribime|ja|多紀理毘売命}}
* {{ill|Ichikishima-hime|ja|市寸島比売命}}
* {{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|多岐都比売命}}

Certain shrines enshrine different deities. For example, at {{ill|Yasaka Shrine|en|Yasaka Shrine|qid=Q692714|lt=Yasaka Shrine}}, the eight princes are identified as [[Yashimajinumi]], {{ill|Isotakeru-no-Mikoto|ja|五十猛神|simple|User:Immanuelle/Isotakeru-no-kami|en:draft|10=fr|11=Isotakeru-no-kami|qid=Q10881556|lt=Isotakeru-no-kami|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isotakeru-no-Mikoto1=Isotakeru-no-Mikoto}}, and other deities.

{{ill|11|ja|大将軍八神社}} identifies the two as such

* {{ill|Taisaijin|ja|太歳神|zh|太歲神|qid=Q10941586}} ({{ill|Ame-no-oshihomimi|de|Amenooshihomimi|fa|آمه-نو-اوشیهومیمی|fr|Ame-no-oshihomimi|it|Ame-no-oshihomimi|ja|アメノオシホミミ|ko|아메노오시호미미|mni|ꯑꯃꯦ-ꯅꯣ-ꯑꯣꯁꯤꯍꯣꯃꯤꯃꯤ|ru|Амэноосихомими но Микото|th|อาเมะ โนะ โอชิโฮมิมิ|uk|Аменоосіхомімі но Мікото|zh|天忍穗耳尊|qid=Q462555|lt=Ame-no-oshihomimi}})
* {{ill|Taionjin|ja|太陰神}} ({{ill|Ichikishima-hime|ja|市杵嶋姫命}})
* {{ill|Saigyōshin|ja|歳刑神}} ({{ill|Tagorihime|ja|田心媛命}})
* {{ill|Saiha Shin|ja|歳破神}} ({{ill|Tagitsuhime|ja|湍津姫命}})
* {{ill|Saisetsujin|ja|歳殺神}} ({{ill|Ame no Hohi|ja|天穂日神}})
* {{ill|Ōbanjin|ja|黄幡神}} ({{ill|Ikutsuhikone|ja|活津彦根神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikutsuhikone|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イクツヒコネ|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11147583}})

== Origin of Hachioji City ==
The name "Hachioji City" originated during the Sengoku period when {{ill|Hōjō Ujiteru|en|Hōjō Ujiteru|qid=Q2790462|lt=Hōjō Ujiteru}} named his castle {{ill|Hachiōji Castle|en|Hachiōji Castle|qid=Q2969389|lt=Hachioji Castle}} after the legends of the eight princes.
